## 10. Interest Diversion Mechanism

An interest diversion mechanism may apply when the transaction satisfies specified collateral-quality conditions but requires additional protection for senior classes. Excess interest proceeds can be diverted toward principal or collateral enhancement rather than distributed to subordinated interests.

The calculation agent determines the applicable test using the collateral balance, eligible collateral, required thresholds and other transaction variables. The manager may be restricted from making discretionary distributions while a required condition remains unsatisfied.

## 11. Priority of Interest Proceeds

Interest proceeds are applied in a defined order of priority. Subject to the governing documents, the sequence generally begins with taxes and senior administrative expenses, followed by trustee and agency expenses, management-related amounts, senior note interest and then junior note interest.

If coverage or diversion tests are failing, the waterfall may redirect otherwise available cash away from junior distributions. Residual interest proceeds are distributed to subordinated interests only after the required senior obligations and applicable reserves have been satisfied.

## 12. Priority of Principal Proceeds

Principal proceeds collected from loan repayments, asset sales and other principal sources are available for reinvestment during the reinvestment period if the transaction conditions permit. Following the reinvestment period, principal proceeds are generally applied sequentially to the rated notes according to their priority.

The principal waterfall may change following an event of default, an optional redemption, a refinancing or another specified transaction event. Equity and subordinated interests receive residual principal only after higher-ranking obligations have been satisfied.

## 13. Reinvestment and Trading Provisions

The reinvestment period is **30 months**. During this period, the manager may use principal proceeds to acquire eligible collateral, subject to the portfolio eligibility criteria, concentration limits, collateral-quality tests and coverage tests.

The manager may also sell or substitute assets when permitted. Trading decisions must consider the effect of the proposed transaction on weighted average spread, weighted average life, rating metrics, diversity, concentration limits and coverage tests.

After the reinvestment period terminates, principal proceeds are generally directed toward deleveraging rather than ordinary reinvestment, subject to limited permitted trading and substitution provisions.

## 14. Optional Redemption, Refinancing and Reset

The transaction includes a non-call period of **12 months**. Following the applicable non-call period, the notes may be subject to optional redemption, refinancing, repricing or reset if the required conditions and voting thresholds are satisfied.

A clean-up call may also be available when the outstanding collateral balance falls below a specified percentage of its original balance. Redemption proceeds are allocated according to the applicable priority of payments.

## 15. Fees, Expenses and Administrative Costs

Transaction expenses include management fees, trustee and administrative fees, collateral administration fees, rating expenses, legal expenses and other costs associated with maintaining the transaction.

The collateral manager receives a management fee subject to the applicable waterfall and fee cap. Senior transaction expenses generally receive priority over junior distributions.

## 16. Collateral Manager Authority and Restrictions

The collateral manager has authority to select, acquire, sell and reinvest collateral within the permitted investment guidelines. The manager must observe eligibility, concentration, collateral-quality and coverage requirements.

Manager powers are constrained by prohibited-investment rules, conflicts provisions, trading restrictions, valuation requirements and transaction tests. Replacement or termination of the manager may occur following specified events and voting procedures.

## 17. Events of Default and Enforcement

Events of default may include failure to make required payments, specified breaches of transaction documents, insolvency-related events and other defined defaults. Following an event of default, the trustee and eligible noteholders may exercise specified remedies.

Remedies can include acceleration, enforcement against transaction assets and application of proceeds under a post-default waterfall. The rights of each note class remain subject to the priority and voting provisions of the transaction documents.

## 18. Voting, Consent and Amendment Matters

Certain amendments require approval from holders of specified classes or percentages of outstanding notes. Extraordinary matters may require higher consent thresholds than routine administrative amendments.

Class voting rights are generally designed to protect the economic interests of each tranche. Subordinated interests may have separate rights on manager replacement, redemption, refinancing or other matters where permitted.

## 19. Reporting, Calculation and Administration

The trustee and collateral administrator prepare or distribute periodic reports containing collateral balances, transaction tests, note balances, payments and other investor information.

Reports may include monthly collateral information, quarterly payment-date calculations, coverage-test results, portfolio statistics and transaction-level compliance information. The calculation agent is responsible for determining specified tests and payment amounts under the governing documents.

## 20. Key Transaction Risks

Investors are exposed to credit losses, defaults, recoveries below expectations, interest-rate movements, reinvestment risk, liquidity risk, concentration risk and counterparty risk. The value and cash flow of the notes depend on the performance of the underlying collateral.

Additional risks arise from manager discretion, structural subordination, coverage-test breaches, refinancing conditions, changes in market liquidity, changes in law or regulation and potential conflicts among different classes of investors.

The subordinated and equity interests generally bear losses before senior noteholders and may receive no distributions in periods of weak collateral performance.

## 21. Selected Definitions

**Overcollateralization (OC):** A ratio comparing the collateral value or adjusted collateral balance with the principal amount of specified classes of notes.

**Interest Coverage (IC):** A ratio comparing available interest proceeds with the interest obligations of specified note classes.

**Reinvestment Period:** The period during which principal proceeds may generally be reinvested in eligible collateral, subject to transaction conditions.

**Non-Call Period:** The initial period during which specified optional redemption rights are restricted.

**Interest Proceeds:** Cash flows attributable to interest and other income from the collateral.

**Principal Proceeds:** Cash flows attributable to principal repayment, sales and other principal sources.

**Defaulted Obligation:** A collateral obligation meeting the transaction's contractual definition of default.

**Weighted Average Spread:** A portfolio-level measure of the weighted average spread earned by the collateral.

**Weighted Average Life:** A weighted estimate of the remaining principal repayment timing of portfolio assets.

**Diversity Score:** A measure used to evaluate portfolio diversification across obligors and industries.

**Collateral Principal Balance:** The amount of collateral principal recognized for transaction calculations after applying applicable adjustments.

**Interest Diversion Test:** A transaction test that may redirect interest proceeds toward principal or senior protection when specified conditions apply.

### 7.2 Operation of limits

A non-voluntary breach is generally addressed through a cure period and trading restrictions rather than an automatic default.

The manager may not knowingly acquire an asset that would cause a concentration category to exceed its contractual limit unless the acquisition is permitted under an express cure, substitution or other exception. When a breach exists, sales or substitutions are selected with regard to liquidity, spread preservation and the need to restore compliance.

## 8. Collateral Quality and Portfolio Tests

### 8.1 Quality benchmarks

The principal quality tests are designed to prevent the manager from improving one portfolio characteristic by materially weakening another. The Effective Date WARF is 2,910 against a maximum target of 3,150. The portfolio's WAS of 3.48% exceeds the 3.25% minimum, while WAC of 7.64% exceeds the 7.00% minimum. CCC or lower assets are limited to 7.0%; excess exposure may receive reduced credit in the adjusted collateral calculation.

Current-pay assets are separately monitored because an obligation can remain current while its market value and credit quality deteriorate. ### 9.2 Failure mechanics

An OC failure generally diverts principal away from junior distributions and toward the most senior affected class. If Class A OC is below its threshold, principal otherwise available for Classes B through E or subordinated interests is redirected in the manner required to restore senior protection. The diversion continues until the test is cured or the relevant principal proceeds are exhausted.

IC failures operate through the Interest Waterfall. Interest otherwise available to subordinated interests can be redirected to affected rated classes. A test failure is therefore economically meaningful even if the portfolio has not experienced a realized default, because cash can be trapped or redirected based on the defined test formulas.

### 9.3 Testing frequency and cures

The OC and IC tests are calculated on each Payment Date and may also be calculated at other times when required by a redemption, refinancing, event of default or other transaction event. A cure is achieved when the applicable test again satisfies its required level under the contractual definitions; simply receiving a favorable market quote does not by itself constitute a cure unless that value enters the defined calculation.

## 10. Interest Diversion Test

### 10.1 Test mechanics

During the Reinvestment Period, the Transaction uses an Interest Diversion Test with a required level of 104.0%. The Calculation Agent compares specified collateral quality and coverage inputs against the benchmark in the indenture on each Payment Date. The test is distinct from the IC tests and is intended to protect the capital structure while allowing the manager to continue reinvesting.

### 10.2 Consequence of a failure

When the Interest Diversion Test is below 104.0%, the specified portion of excess interest otherwise distributable to subordinated interests is recharacterized as Principal Proceeds. During the Reinvestment Period, those proceeds may be used for eligible reinvestment if the applicable criteria are satisfied; otherwise they are applied through the permitted principal priority. The diversion ceases once the test is cured.

## 11. Priority of Interest Payments

### 11.1 Interest waterfall

Interest Proceeds are applied in a defined sequence. First, the Issuer pays taxes, registered-office expenses and other senior administrative amounts. Second, trustee, calculation, paying-agent, collateral-administration and custody expenses are paid. Third, the management fee and permitted hedge or counterparty amounts are paid. The remaining distributable interest then pays Class A-1, Class A-2, Class B, Class C, Class D and Class E, subject to any required coverage-test diversion or interest deferral.

Only after the required rated-note obligations and specified diversions have been satisfied may residual interest be distributed to subordinated interests. The ordering is contractual and should not be inferred solely from the relative ratings of the notes.

### 11.2 Interest shortfalls

If available Interest Proceeds are insufficient to pay a class in full, the shortfall is allocated according to the transaction's priority rules. A junior interest shortfall can occur without a senior interest shortfall. Where the documents permit deferral, the unpaid amount remains subject to the applicable subsequent-period provisions.

## 12. Principal Waterfall and Reinvestment Policy

### 12.1 Principal during the Reinvestment Period

Principal Proceeds consist principally of scheduled amortization, collateral sale proceeds, recoveries and other amounts treated as principal. Until January 20, 2030, the manager may reinvest qualifying Principal Proceeds in Eligible Collateral Obligations. Reinvestment must maintain or satisfy the required portfolio tests, concentration limits and maturity restrictions.

### 12.2 Trading and substitution

Asset sales may be undertaken to capture gains, improve credit quality, reduce concentration, manage liquidity, respond to rating changes or address documentation issues. Substitutions may be used where an asset becomes unsuitable, subject to the applicable eligibility and concentration rules. The manager may not use a series of trades to circumvent a contractual limit.

### 12.3 After the Reinvestment Period

After January 20, 2030, principal is generally applied sequentially to Class A-1 and Class A-2, followed by Classes B, C, D and E. Subordinated interests receive the residual only after required note principal and expenses have been paid. Post-reinvestment sales remain possible for workouts, credit deterioration, permitted substitutions, clean-up activity and other specified purposes, but ordinary portfolio turnover is reduced.

## 13. Redemption, Refinancing and Reset Provisions

### 13.1 Optional redemption

The subordinated interest holders may direct an optional redemption after the Non-call Period, subject to the applicable notice, minimum amount and payment conditions. The Non-call Period ends November 20, 2027. A clean-up call is available when the collateral balance falls below 10% of its original amount, subject to sufficient proceeds to satisfy the applicable redemption price and expenses.

### 13.2 Refinancing and repricing

Following the Non-call Period, the transaction may permit refinancing of one or more classes, or a repricing that changes the spread of selected notes. Such action requires satisfaction of the consent, pricing, notice and non-impairment conditions. A partial refinancing cannot reorder the seniority of a non-consenting class unless the governing provisions expressly allow it.

### 13.3 Reset feature

A reset may extend or modify the Reinvestment Period or alter selected portfolio and capital-structure terms if the required class and subordinated-holder approvals are obtained. A reset is not automatic and cannot eliminate protected noteholder rights without the specified extraordinary consent.

## 14. Fees, Expenses and Transaction Costs

### 14.1 Management compensation

The base management fee is 0.30% per annum of the relevant collateral balance during the Reinvestment Period and 0.27% thereafter. A performance allocation of up to 7.5% of residual distributions may be payable after the contractual hurdle. The performance allocation is subordinate to required note interest, principal and coverage-test diversions.

### 14.2 Administrative expenses

Summit Ridge Trust Company receives a base annual trustee and agency fee of $96,000 plus permitted extraordinary expenses. Collateral administration is budgeted at $72,000 annually plus transaction-based charges. Rating expenses, legal fees, audit costs, custody fees, tax services, placement expenses and permitted hedge costs are paid according to their assigned priority. Enforcement, restructuring and contested legal matters can produce significant additional expenses.

## 15. Manager Powers, Restrictions and Conflicts

### 15.1 Trading authority

BlueRiver Asset Management LLC may purchase, sell, amend, waive, exchange, restructure and otherwise manage collateral within the transaction's investment guidelines. It may participate in lender votes and workouts and may use permitted cash-management investments for temporary liquidity.

### 15.2 Restrictions

The manager may not knowingly acquire an ineligible asset, breach a concentration limit without a permitted exception, or structure trades principally to evade a portfolio test. Maturity, currency, rating, spread and asset-type restrictions apply at the time of purchase. Affiliate transactions must be handled under the conflict and allocation procedures.

### 15.3 Conflicts and manager replacement

BlueRiver Asset Management LLC and its affiliates may manage other accounts that own similar loans. Allocation procedures are intended to address competing opportunities, but they do not ensure equal allocations. A manager may be terminated following specified events, including uncured material breach, insolvency or certain regulatory events. Replacement generally requires satisfaction of the eligibility standard and any applicable noteholder or equity-holder approval.

## 16. Events of Default and Remedies

### 16.1 Events of default

Events of default include specified failures to pay senior principal or interest after applicable grace periods, insolvency of the Issuer or Co-Issuer, and material breaches of covenants that remain uncured. Certain permitted deferrals of junior interest are expressly excluded from payment-default provisions.

### 16.2 Acceleration and enforcement

Following an Event of Default and any required direction, the Trustee may accelerate the notes, enforce security over the collateral, sell assets and take other permitted remedies. Enforcement proceeds are applied through the post-acceleration waterfall, which preserves seniority and gives senior noteholders priority over junior classes and subordinated interests.

Noteholders have rights to receive required payments, receive reports and vote on matters assigned to them. Trustee remedies are subject to applicable standards of care, indemnification, direction and limitation provisions.

## 17. Voting, Amendments and Consent Rights

### 17.1 Voting thresholds

Ordinary amendments generally require consent of holders representing more than 50% of the affected voting balance. Extraordinary matters generally require 75% or more, and certain class-specific changes require a separate vote of the affected class. Protected matters include reductions of principal, reductions of stated interest, changes in payment priority, extensions of legal final maturity and changes to core noteholder protections.

### 17.2 Equity-holder rights

Subordinated interest holders have specified rights to direct optional redemption and participate in manager and administrative decisions assigned to them. These rights do not permit them to amend protected senior noteholder economics without the required senior consent.

### 17.3 Manager replacement

Manager replacement may be initiated under specified circumstances through the voting procedures. The replacement process is intended to preserve portfolio continuity and requires the proposed manager to accept the investment restrictions and reporting obligations of the Transaction.

## 18. Reporting, Valuation and Calculation Responsibilities

### 18.1 Monthly collateral reporting

Monthly reports are expected to identify collateral obligors, balances, ratings, prices, spreads, coupons, maturities, industry classifications, geographic information and default status. Aggregate reports include WAS, WAC, WARF, WAL, diversity, recovery assumptions, concentration levels and trading activity.

### 18.2 Payment Date and quarterly reporting

On each Payment Date, the Trustee and Calculation Agent produce a Payment Date Report showing Interest Proceeds, Principal Proceeds, expenses, note interest, principal distributions, coverage-test results, Interest Diversion Test results and ending note balances. Quarterly investor reporting provides additional portfolio commentary and valuation information.

### 18.3 Valuation process

Where observable market quotations are available, they are used under the permitted valuation hierarchy. Otherwise, the manager may rely on dealer indications, comparable instruments, cash-flow analysis or another approved methodology. Valuation estimates can differ materially from actual sale proceeds, particularly during stressed or illiquid markets.

The Calculation Agent is responsible for applying contractual formulas, not for independently validating every underlying commercial fact. The manager supplies portfolio information and trade records, while the Trustee maintains official transaction books and records.

## 19. Risk Factors

### 19.1 Credit and default risk

The collateral consists principally of below-investment-grade corporate obligations. Defaults, restructurings, downgrades and covenant breaches can reduce cash flow and collateral value. A portfolio recovery rate below the 52.5% assumption can increase losses to junior notes and subordinated interests and may trigger coverage-test diversions.

### 19.2 Recovery and concentration risk

Recovery depends on enterprise value, collateral ranking, documentation, competing creditors and market conditions. Concentration limits reduce but do not eliminate exposure to correlated defaults. Industry and geographic stress can cause multiple obligors to deteriorate simultaneously.

### 19.3 Interest-rate and reinvestment risk

Most collateral and notes are floating-rate, but their spreads, floors and reset conventions differ. Changes in Term SOFR can alter both asset income and note expense. During the 36-month Reinvestment Period, replacement assets may offer lower spreads, longer lives or weaker credit quality.

### 19.4 Liquidity and market-value risk

Loans may trade infrequently. The manager may be unable to sell an asset at a desired price or within the period required to cure a concentration or credit problem. Market-value declines can affect collateral tests even without realized defaults.

### 19.5 Counterparty and operational risk

Trustee, custodian, hedge-counterparty, administrator or account-bank failure could disrupt cash management. Operational errors in settlement, reporting or calculation may require correction and can create timing risk.

### 19.6 Structural, subordination and redemption risk

The notes are structurally subordinated according to their class priority. A coverage-test failure can divert cash from junior classes. Optional redemption or refinancing may repay notes earlier than expected, while market conditions may prevent refinancing and leave the securities outstanding longer.

### 19.7 Manager and regulatory risk

Performance depends partly on the manager's credit selection, trading and workout decisions. Regulatory, tax, accounting or capital-rule changes could affect transaction economics. Non-U.S.-dollar assets also create foreign-exchange and hedging risk.

## 20. Defined Terms

### 20.1 Structural definitions

Collateral Principal Balance means the principal amount of collateral recognized under the Transaction's defined calculation rules. Adjusted Collateral Principal Balance means that balance after specified adjustments for defaulted, discounted, low-rated or otherwise specially treated assets. Effective Date is January 8, 2027.

Reinvestment Period is the period ending January 20, 2030 during which qualifying Principal Proceeds may generally be reinvested. Non-call Period is the period ending November 20, 2027 during which ordinary optional redemption is restricted.

### 20.2 Cash-flow and coverage definitions

Interest Proceeds are amounts treated as interest under the transaction documents. Principal Proceeds are amounts treated as principal, including permitted sale proceeds and recoveries. OC means overcollateralization, generally the ratio of recognized collateral to specified note balances. IC means interest coverage, comparing specified Interest Proceeds with required interest obligations.

CCC Assets are obligations rated CCC/Caa or lower under the applicable rating methodology. Defaulted Obligations are assets meeting the defined default criteria. Coverage Tests include the OC and IC tests. Interest Diversion Test is the separate test that can redirect otherwise distributable interest during the Reinvestment Period.

### 20.3 Portfolio metrics

WARF means Weighted Average Rating Factor. WAS means Weighted Average Spread. WAL means Weighted Average Life. A portfolio statistic is not automatically the same as a contractual test value; the definitions determine which assets and adjustments enter each calculation.

## 21. Illustrative Operating Outcomes

### 21.1 Normal Payment Date

If the Transaction remains in compliance, Interest Proceeds first satisfy taxes and administrative expenses, then trustee and transaction fees, management and permitted hedge payments, followed by rated-note interest. Principal collected during the Reinvestment Period is generally available for qualifying reinvestment. Residual distributions are made only after required diversions and rated obligations.

### 21.2 Class C OC deficiency

If Class A and Class B OC tests pass but Class C OC falls below 113.0%, principal otherwise available for junior classes or subordinated interests can be redirected toward the affected classes. The manager may also be restricted from purchasing assets that would increase the deficiency. Once the defined test is restored, ordinary principal distribution can resume.

### 21.3 Interest Diversion deficiency

If the Interest Diversion Test falls below 104.0%, the specified portion of excess interest otherwise available to subordinated interests is redirected. During the Reinvestment Period the diverted amount may support qualifying purchases or follow the permitted principal application, depending on the applicable cure conditions.

## 22. Transaction Distinctions and Retrieval Anchors

BlueRiver CLO 2026-2 has a $650 million target collateral balance, a 36-month Reinvestment Period, a 7.0% CCC/lower concentration limit, a 52.5% initial recovery assumption and a 66.4 diversity score. These figures are deliberately specific retrieval anchors. The Effective Date is January 8, 2027, while the Closing Date is November 13, 2026.

The Transaction's defined Class A OC trigger is 128.5%, compared with 119.0% for Class B, 113.0% for Class C and 108.0% for Class D. The Interest Diversion Test threshold is 104.0%. These thresholds should not be confused with the portfolio's headline collateral-to-note ratio because the contractual tests use defined adjustments.

The transaction also deliberately separates the Non-call Period from the Reinvestment Period. Optional redemption is restricted through November 20, 2027, whereas active reinvestment can continue through January 20, 2030. The legal final maturity is November 20, 2041, substantially later than the weighted average maturity of the initial collateral.

This structure is designed for hierarchical retrieval: transaction overview facts occur in high-level sections; detailed eligibility and concentration rules occur under nested headings; coverage and waterfall mechanics are described in narrative; and selected portfolio and capital-structure facts appear in compact tables. The document is wholly synthetic.

End of BlueRiver CLO 2026-2 synthetic transaction document.

Certain actions require direction from the requisite noteholders and may be subject to indemnification and other trustee protections.

### 17.3 Post-acceleration priority

After acceleration, proceeds are applied through the enforcement waterfall. Senior expenses and obligations are addressed before senior notes, followed by junior rated classes and finally Subordinated Interests. The post-acceleration waterfall does not permit subordinated interests to bypass senior noteholder claims.

## 18. Voting and Amendment Provisions

### 18.1 Ordinary amendments

Ordinary amendments generally require consent from holders of more than 50% of the affected voting balance. Matters affecting only one class may require a separate class vote. Amendments may address administrative provisions, reporting mechanics and other permitted matters without necessarily requiring unanimous consent.

### 18.2 Extraordinary matters

Extraordinary matters generally require at least 75% consent of the affected voting interests, with higher or class-specific requirements for protected economic terms. These include reductions of principal or stated interest, changes to payment priority, extensions of Legal Final Maturity and amendments that materially impair noteholder rights.

### 18.3 Manager replacement and equity rights

Subordinated Interests have specified voting and direction rights, including rights associated with optional redemption and certain manager matters. Such rights remain subject to protected noteholder provisions. Manager replacement requires the applicable vote and a successor satisfying the contractual eligibility requirements.

## 19. Reporting, Valuation and Administration

### 19.1 Monthly reports

The monthly collateral report identifies individual assets, obligors, balances, ratings, prices, spreads, coupons, maturities, industry classifications, geography and default status. Aggregate metrics include WARF, WAS, WAC, WAL, diversity score, recovery assumptions and concentration percentages.

### 19.2 Payment Date reporting

On each Payment Date, the Calculation Agent and Trustee prepare a report showing Interest Proceeds, Principal Proceeds, fees, note interest, principal distributions, OC and IC results, the Interest Diversion Test, and ending balances. Quarterly reports include additional portfolio commentary and valuation information.

### 19.3 Valuation and calculations

Observable market quotations are used where available under the defined valuation hierarchy. When direct quotations are not available, permitted dealer indications, comparable instruments and cash-flow analysis may be used. Valuation is an estimate and may differ materially from liquidation proceeds during stressed markets.

The Calculation Agent applies the contractual formulas. The Collateral Manager supplies trade and portfolio information, while the Trustee maintains official transaction books and records. Reporting discrepancies are corrected through the procedures specified in the transaction documents.

## 20. Risk Factors

### 20.1 Credit, default and recovery risk

The portfolio consists primarily of below-investment-grade corporate obligations. Borrower defaults, restructurings, downgrades and covenant breaches may reduce Interest Proceeds and Principal Proceeds. Recoveries may be below the 53.0% initial assumption, especially where enterprise values decline or collateral is subordinated to other claims.

### 20.2 Interest-rate and reinvestment risk

Most collateral and all rated notes use floating-rate mechanics, but asset spreads, floors and reset dates can differ. Changes in Term SOFR can alter net interest margins. During the 30-month Reinvestment Period, replacement assets may carry lower spreads, longer maturities or weaker ratings than assets originally purchased.

### 20.3 Liquidity and concentration risk

Loans may be illiquid and may not be saleable at the price assumed by the manager. Concentration limits reduce but do not eliminate correlated losses. Industry, geographic and sponsor-level stress can affect multiple obligors simultaneously.

### 20.4 Counterparty and operational risk

Failure of a trustee, custodian, account bank, hedge counterparty or service provider could interrupt payments or reporting. Operational errors can create timing mismatches or require correction. The transaction depends on accurate data from multiple parties.

### 20.5 Structural and subordination risk

The capital structure allocates losses in order from Subordinated Interests through the rated classes. Coverage-test failures can redirect cash away from junior investors. Senior noteholders may be paid while junior classes receive reduced or no distributions.

### 20.6 Redemption, manager and regulatory risk

Optional redemption can shorten the expected life of the notes, while market conditions can make refinancing uneconomic. The manager's investment and workout decisions materially affect performance. Changes in tax, securities, banking or regulatory requirements may alter transaction costs or permitted activities.

### 20.7 Foreign-currency risk

Permitted non-U.S.-dollar assets can create foreign-exchange exposure. Hedging arrangements reduce but may not eliminate basis, timing and counterparty risk. Currency movements can affect the realized value of otherwise eligible collateral.

## 21. Definitions and Glossary

### 21.1 Structural terms

Collateral Principal Balance means the principal amount of collateral recognized under the Transaction's defined rules. Adjusted Collateral Principal Balance means the Collateral Principal Balance after contractual adjustments for specified defaults, discounts, low-rated assets and other special categories. Effective Date means November 6, 2026.

Reinvestment Period means the period ending May 20, 2029 during which qualifying Principal Proceeds may generally be reinvested. Non-call Period means the period ending September 20, 2027 during which ordinary optional redemption is restricted. Legal Final Maturity means September 20, 2041.

### 21.2 Cash-flow and test terms

Interest Proceeds are amounts treated as interest under the transaction documents. Principal Proceeds are amounts treated as principal. OC means overcollateralization and generally compares recognized collateral to specified note balances. IC means interest coverage and compares specified Interest Proceeds with required interest obligations.

CCC Assets are obligations rated CCC/Caa or lower under the applicable rating framework. Defaulted Obligations are assets meeting the defined default criteria. Coverage Tests include the OC and IC tests. Interest Diversion Test is the separate 103.5% test that can redirect specified excess interest during the Reinvestment Period.

### 21.3 Portfolio metrics

WARF means Weighted Average Rating Factor. WAS means Weighted Average Spread. WAL means Weighted Average Life. These measures are calculated according to transaction-specific definitions and should not be treated as interchangeable with headline portfolio statistics.

## 22. Illustrative Payment-Date Scenarios

### 22.1 Normal compliance

In a normal quarter, Interest Proceeds first satisfy senior administrative expenses and transaction-party fees, followed by the management fee and permitted hedge amounts. Rated-note interest is then paid through the Interest Waterfall. During the Reinvestment Period, Principal Proceeds can be reinvested when all applicable criteria are satisfied.

### 22.2 Class C OC deficiency

Suppose the Class C OC ratio declines below its 113.5% requirement while Classes A and B remain compliant. Principal otherwise available to junior classes or Subordinated Interests can be redirected toward the affected class under the principal priority. The manager may also be restricted from purchasing assets that worsen the deficiency.

### 22.3 Interest Diversion Test deficiency

If the Interest Diversion Test falls below 103.5%, specified excess interest is redirected into Principal Proceeds. During the Reinvestment Period, the amount may support qualifying reinvestment if permitted. The diversion ceases after the contractual test is restored.

### 22.4 Post-reinvestment operation

After May 20, 2029, ordinary reinvestment ends and principal is generally applied sequentially to the rated classes. The manager continues to manage defaults, workouts and permitted substitutions, but its trading mandate is materially narrower than during the Reinvestment Period.

### 24.1 Source hierarchy for transaction calculations

For purposes of internal administration, the transaction distinguishes among collateral-level source data, manager portfolio records, the Calculation Agent's test calculations and the Trustee's official books. A collateral record may contain borrower name, facility type, commitment, funded amount, spread, floor, price, maturity, rating, industry and geographic classification. The manager reconciles these records to trade confirmations and settlement records before the periodic portfolio report is finalized.

### 24.2 Treatment of changes after reporting

If a rating, balance, price or default status changes after a report is prepared, the subsequent report reflects the updated information according to the applicable cut-off. Corrections to historical reports are handled under the administrative procedures and do not automatically alter prior distributions unless the governing documents require a recalculation.

### 24.3 Cash and temporary investments

Cash pending reinvestment may be held in permitted short-dated investments or transaction accounts. Such assets are subject to counterparty and liquidity requirements and are not treated as substitutes for diversified loan collateral for purposes of every portfolio-quality test. The manager is responsible for maintaining sufficient liquidity for expected settlement obligations and permitted draws.

When an obligor enters financial distress, Oakmont may negotiate amendments, waivers, exchanges or restructurings. ## 4. Coverage Tests and Cash Flow Application

### 4.1 Overcollateralization (OC) and Interest Coverage (IC) Tests

The transaction features robust structural protections. The Class A/B OC Test is set at 123.0%, ensuring that for every $100 of senior debt, there is at least $123 of collateral value (as adjusted for defaults and CCC assets). The Class C, D, and E OC tests are set at 115.5%, 110.2%, and 106.0% respectively. The IC Tests, which measure the adequacy of interest collections to pay note interest, are set at 120.0% for the senior notes.

### 4.2 Interest and Principal Waterfalls

On each quarterly Payment Date, the Issuer will apply Interest Proceeds to pay administrative expenses, management fees, and interest on the notes in order of seniority. If a Coverage Test is failed, interest proceeds that would have gone to junior notes or equity are redirected to pay down the principal of the most senior class. Principal Proceeds during the Reinvestment Period are typically used to purchase new assets, while after the Reinvestment Period, they are used to redeem the notes sequentially.

### 4.3 Interest Diversion Test

Unique to the Reinvestment Period, the Interest Diversion Test is a 'soft' trigger. If the Class E OC Ratio falls below 107.0%, the Issuer must divert 50% of available excess interest to the Principal Collection Account for the purchase of additional Collateral Obligations, rather than distributing it to the Subordinated Noteholders.

## 5. Investment Risk Considerations

Investors should consider the following risks: (1) Credit Risk: The risk that borrowers of the underlying loans will fail to make payments. (2) Market Value Risk: The risk that the market price of the collateral will decline, potentially triggering 'discounted obligation' haircuts. (3) Reinvestment Risk: The risk that the Manager will be unable to find replacement assets with sufficient yield during the 5-year reinvestment window. (4) Structural Risk: The risk that the sequential priority of payments will leave junior and subordinated holders with no recovery in a stress scenario.

### 5.1 Legal Final Maturity

The Legal Final Maturity of the notes is October 20, 2038. Noteholders should be aware that the actual life of the notes may be significantly shorter due to prepayments on the underlying loans or an optional redemption by the Subordinated Noteholders following the non-call period.

## 6. Glossary of Transaction Terms

Adjusted Collateral Principal Balance: The aggregate principal balance of the portfolio, minus haircuts for defaulted assets, long-dated assets, and excess CCC/Caa assets.

Defaulted Obligation: Any asset for which the obligor is in bankruptcy or has failed to pay interest or principal for a period exceeding the relevant grace period.

Effective Date: The date (March 28, 2027) by which the Manager must have substantially invested the Target Portfolio balance.

Reinvestment Period: The period during which the Manager may buy and sell assets, ending on the Payment Date in October 2031.

WARF (Weighted Average Rating Factor): A measure of the default probability of the portfolio as assigned by the Rating Agencies.

## 10. Principal Waterfall

Principal proceeds include principal repayments, sale proceeds treated as principal and other principal collections. During the reinvestment period, principal proceeds can be used for permitted reinvestments.

After the reinvestment period, available principal is generally applied sequentially to the rated notes, beginning with Class A-1 and then moving through the capital structure. Principal distributions to subordinated interests are residual and occur only after higher-ranking obligations have been satisfied.

Following an event of default or certain optional redemption events, the principal waterfall can operate under a different priority. The post-default provisions are designed to preserve the relative priority of the note classes while enabling enforcement and liquidation of collateral.

## 11. Reinvestment Mechanics

### Trading during the reinvestment period

The reinvestment period runs from June 30, 2026 through June 30, 2029, subject to the transaction's stated termination conventions. During this period, the manager may reinvest principal proceeds in eligible collateral and may sell assets for permitted reasons.

Permitted trading includes replacing an asset with another eligible asset, improving portfolio quality, managing concentration, responding to borrower events and maintaining compliance with collateral tests. A trade cannot be evaluated solely on spread: the manager must also consider maturity, rating, diversity, industry exposure, asset type and the effect on coverage tests.

### Post-reinvestment period

After June 30, 2029, ordinary reinvestment generally ceases. Limited sales and substitutions can continue where permitted, but principal collections are principally directed toward deleveraging. The manager may still be required to dispose of assets to address defaults, concentration breaches or other specified events.

## 12. Redemption, Refinancing and Reset

The non-call period is 15 months from the closing date. After the non-call period, the subordinated interests may, subject to required conditions, direct an optional redemption or refinancing of the rated notes.

A clean-up call may be exercised if the aggregate collateral principal balance falls below 10% of the original collateral balance , provided the other contractual conditions are met. Refinancing or repricing may require specified noteholder consents and satisfaction of applicable economic and documentation conditions.

A reset transaction may extend the reinvestment period or modify selected economic terms if the required classes approve the transaction. The rights of the subordinated interests are subject to the voting and conflict provisions of the governing documents.

## 15. Events of Default and Remedies

After acceleration, proceeds from collateral liquidation are distributed under the applicable post-default waterfall. Subordinated interests generally remain last in priority and can suffer a complete loss before senior classes are impaired.
